entries.title: I Corinthians 11:1
segments: ¶Be my imitators, even as *I* also [am] of Christ.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:2
segments: Now I praise you, that in all things ye are mindful of me; and that as I have directed you, ye keep the directions.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:3
segments: But I wish you to know that the Christ is the head of every man, but woman's head [is] the man, and the Christ's head God.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:4
segments: Every man praying or prophesying, having [anything] on his head, puts his head to shame.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:5
segments: But every woman praying or prophesying with her head uncovered puts her own head to shame; for it is one and the same as a shaved [woman].

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:6
segments: For if a woman be not covered, let her hair also be cut off. But if [it be] shameful to a woman to have her hair cut off or to be shaved, let her be covered.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:7
segments: For man indeed ought not to have his head covered, being God's image and glory; but woman is man's glory.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:8
segments: For man is not of woman, but woman of man.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:9
segments: For also man was not created for the sake of the woman, but woman for the sake of the man.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:10
segments: Therefore ought the woman to have authority on her head, on account of the angels.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:11
segments: However, neither [is] woman without man, nor man without woman, in [the] Lord.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:12
segments: For as the woman [is] of the man, so also [is] the man by the woman, but all things of God.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:13
segments: Judge in yourselves: is it comely that a woman should pray to God uncovered?

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:14
segments: Does not even nature itself teach you, that man, if he have long hair, it is a dishonour to him?

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:15
segments: But woman, if she have long hair, [it is] glory to her; for the long hair is given [to her] in lieu of a veil.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:16
segments: But if any one think to be contentious, *we* have no such custom, nor the assemblies of God.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:17
segments: ¶But [in] prescribing [to you on] this [which I now enter on], I do not praise, [namely,] that ye come together, not for the better, but for the worse.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:18
segments: For first, when ye come together in assembly, I hear there exist divisions among you, and I partly give credit [to it].

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:19
segments: For there must also be sects among you, that the approved may become manifest among you.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:20
segments: When ye come therefore together into one place, it is not to eat [the] Lord's supper.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:21
segments: For each one in eating takes his *own* supper before [others], and one is hungry and another drinks to excess.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:22
segments: Have ye not then houses for eating and drinking? or do ye despise the assembly of God, and put to shame them who have not? What shall I say to you? shall I praise you? In this [point] I do not praise.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:23
segments: ¶For *I* received from the Lord, that which I also delivered to you, that the Lord Jesus, in the night in which he was delivered up, took bread,

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:24
segments: and having given thanks broke [it], and said, This is my body, which [is] for you: this do in remembrance of me.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:25
segments: In like manner also the cup, after having supped, saying, This cup is the new covenant in my blood: this do, as often as ye shall drink [it], in remembrance of me.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:26
segments: For as often as ye shall eat this bread, and drink the cup, ye announce the death of the Lord, until he come.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:27
segments: So that whosoever shall eat the bread, or drink the cup of the Lord, unworthily, shall be guilty in respect of the body and of the blood of the Lord.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:28
segments: But let a man prove himself, and thus eat of the bread, and drink of the cup.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:29
segments: For [the] eater and drinker eats and drinks judgment to himself, not distinguishing the body.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:30
segments: On this account many among you [are] weak and infirm, and a good many are fallen asleep.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:31
segments: But if we judged ourselves, so were we not judged.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:32
segments: But being judged, we are disciplined of [the] Lord, that we may not be condemned with the world.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:33
segments: So that, my brethren, when ye come together to eat, wait for one another.

entries.title: I Corinthians 11:34
segments: If any one be hungry, let him eat at home, that ye may not come together for judgment. But the other things, whenever I come, I will set in order.
